title: Signal condensation probe plan and ownership
content:
Purpose:
This note proposes a compact, cost-conscious approach to shaping observation signals for low-noise, high-actionability dashboards and traces. The goal is to shrink signal surface area (aka "signal condensation") so oncall and product teams can find root causes faster while keeping observability query/ingestion cost under control.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: SREs, Runtime eng, Product (hosted API + dedicated).
- Secondary: Solutions eng, CS, Console PM.
- Scope: token-serving paths, routing/fallback flows, and long-tail model fallback events (not full-featured logs or user-level audit events).

Motivation / problem statement:
We have many overlapping panels and long dashboards that take time to read and cost to query. Investigations often involve:
- chasing many high-cardinality metrics (tenant, model, route)
- ad-hoc trace sampling that doesn't capture retry cascades or KV-cache warmness properly
- operators doing repeated expensive queries to reconstruct a session slice

Signal condensation principles (high level):
1) Prioritize session-first signals: try to reconstruct a single diagnostic path per user request rather than many independent counters.
2) Tier signals by operational persona: operator (investigate), product (trend), billing (cost). Each gets a small curated surface.
3) Keep a compact core metric set (~12 metrics) that answers 80% of operator questions.
4) Use lightweight derived signals on ingest (e.g., normalized-token-latency) rather than heavy post-hoc joins.
5) Adaptive trace sampling: bias sampling to requests showing anomaly heuristics rather than uniform sampling.

Core metric inventory (proposed compact set) — for each request/session include the following tags: tenant_id, model_family, route, backend_region, fallback_flag
- request_count: gauge (per-minute rate) — owner: obs-runtime — alert: drops >30% 10m
- p50_token_latency_ms: histogram-derived quantile — owner: obs-runtime — alert: p50 > 80ms for 5m
- p95_token_latency_ms: same — alert: p95 > 350ms (soft)
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: fraction (0-1) — owner: serving-runtime — alert: < 0.6 for top-10 tenants by qps
- cold_start_rate: fraction of requests that required model cold init — owner: infra — alert: >1% sustained (depends on model)
- fallback_rate: fraction of requests that fell back to alternate model/region — owner: routing — alert: >0.5%
- token_cost_per_request: currency-normalized estimate — owner: finance-observability — used in cost dashboards
- rate_limited_requests: count — owner: quotas — alert: spikes vs baseline
- error_rate_class_B: count (user-facing errors) — owner: obs-runtime — alert: >0.1%
- prompt_truncation_rate: fraction of requests truncated by policy/length — owner: console — used for UX metrics
- model_prompt_len_median: median tokens in prompt — owner: product-hosted-api
- inference_tail_probability: derived (p99 of token-emit-counts) — owner: model-ops

Notes on definitions: keep samples consistent — prefer per-request aggregates (one row per request at ingest time) instead of separate token-by-token counters. This makes low-cardinality rollups cheap and keeps dashboards snappy.

Trace sampling and annotation strategy:
- Triggered trace sampling: sample 100% for requests where any of the following is true: fallback_flag == true, error_rate_class_B > 0, cold_start == true, kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.25, token_latency percentiles above thresholds.
- Baseline sampling: ~0.5% uniform sample for global visibility.
- Enrich traces at collection-time with the compact metric set (above) as top-level trace attributes to make trace filtering cheap.
- Trace duration budgets: limit full-span retention for traces that exceed 5s; keep light-weight breadcrumb traces (span skeleton) for medium requests to save storage.
- Span tagging guide (short):
  - span.service = host-layer (e.g., frontend, router, runtime, model-worker)
  - span.op = short op name (tokenize, kv_lookup, kernel_call, reply_stream)
  - trace.user_session = base64(session-id) when available
  - trace.request_flags = comma-separated list (fallback, cold_start, rate_limit)
  - span.kv.bucket = hot|warm|cold when KV check happens

Dashboard composition guidance:
- Keep an "investigation deck" of 6 compact panels per service: request rate, p95 latency heatmap (by route), kv_cache_heatmap, fallback_rate by model_family, error spike list (annotated), cost per 100k tokens.
- Use small-multiple panels for top-10 tenants instead of per-tenant giant dashboards. Provide a tenant selector for deeper slices.
- Persist one synthetic probe per region that exercises the whole stack and writes trace-anchored probes into the system every 5 minutes. These act as a baseline and help calibrate probe-triggered sampling.
- Provide an "operator quickcard" (single row) that contains the top 3 likely causes (cache coldness, routing fallback, kernel congestion) determined by simple heuristics on the compact metric set. Quickcard should link directly to a session trace and to the rollout/PR if applicable.

Cost & ingest considerations:
- Prefer per-request event with ~12 fields over token-level metrics (less cardinality).
- Aggregate heavy histograms at the edge (percentile sketches) before sending to central telemetry.
- Implement light-weight pre-ingest filters to drop or downsample known-noise tenants (internal tests, synthetic storms).

Operational runbook (short):
1) Alert fires (e.g., p95_token_latency breach): check 6-panel investigation deck for region/model anomalies.
2) If fallback_rate high: open routing dashboard and find affected model_family; look at trace sampling bucket for full traces.
3) If kv_cache_hit_ratio degraded: check startup churn (cold_start_rate) and probe traces for eviction patterns.
4) If cost spike: check token_cost_per_request and top tenants, pull recent rollout PRs (link in quickcard).

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- exact thresholds for alerts per model_family (need product/infra signoff).
- canonical session id format across routing/console for consistent trace stitching.
- storage tiering policy for trace skeletons vs full spans (cost model needed).
- how to indicate privacy-sensitive flows (PII) so traces can be redacted earlier.

Action items (owners):
- obs-runtime: prototype per-request ingest proto and percentile sketching (JIRA-OBS-313) — owner: Leah Park — due: 2026-03-05
- serving-runtime: ensure kv bucket tag at kv-lookup spans — owner: Omar Castillo — due: 2026-02-28
- routing: expose fallback_reason enum in router headers — owner: Hannah Liu — due: 2026-03-10
- obs-sre: build operator quickcard prototype in Grafana using the core metric set — owner: Ravi Menon — due: 2026-03-15

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact and opinionated. We want to reduce noise and accelerate mean-time-to-detect. Expect a follow-up doc that maps these compact signals back to full telemetry for compliance/forensics use cases.
- For discussion: tradeoffs between pre-ingest derived signals vs post-hoc derivation (cost vs flexibility).

Slack threads / references: #obs-infra (thread: fallback-cost-2025), https://confluence.redwood.ai/obs/signal-condensation-proposal (placeholder), PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/423
